title: Optimized protocol for direct extraction of SARS-CoV-2 RNA from raw wastewater samples (ANRS 0160)
author: Chaqroun, El Soufi, et al.
materials:
Neutral Phenol-Chloroform(NPC)Treatment (theonly modification to Manufacturer's Protocol)
•Prepare a separation tube in a 50 mL conical tube containing: 4 g of a mixture of high-vacuum silicon grease and silicon dioxide in a 90:10 w/w ratio.•Transfer 15 mL of lysate into the separation tube.•Add 15 mL of phenol-chloroform-isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1 pH 7.8–8.2, Sigma Aldrich, Ref. 77617).•Shake vigorously by hand for 1 min.•Centrifuge at 3500 × g for 5 min.•Transfer 15 mL of the aqueous phase into new 50 mL conical tube.

Option 1: Using NucliSENSⓇ miniMAGTM•Resuspend the silica magnetic beads with 400 µL of Wash Buffer 1 (WB1).•Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL tube and place it in the NucliSENSⓇ miniMAGTM.•Perform two washing steps:-Contact time: 30 s per wash.-Discard fluid via aspiration after each step.•Perform two additional washes with 500 µL of Wash Buffer 2 (WB2):-Contact time: 30 s per wash.-Discard fluid via aspiration after each step.•Perform a final wash with 500 µL of Wash Buffer 3 (WB3):-Contact time: 15 s.-Discard fluid via aspiration after each step.•Remove the 1.5 mL tube from the NucliSENSⓇ miniMAGTM.•Resuspend the silica beads in 50 µL of WB3.•Perform elution at 60 °C for 5 min at 1400 rpm in a Thermomixer comfort (Eppendorf).•Place the tube in a magnetic rack and collect the 50 µL of eluate.

Quantification Using a Standard Curve
•A known target sequence in this case, the SARS-CoV-2 E gene amplicon cloned into a plasmid vector called pCR2.1 (Invitrogen, 452,640) [11] was used for quantification.•This plasmid acts as a reference standard because it contains the exact sequence of interest.•A 10-fold serial dilution of the plasmid is prepared. Each dilution contains a known copy number of the target gene. The diluted plasmid samples are run in RT-qPCR to generate Cq (quantification cycle) values.•A standard curve is plotted with: The logarithm of the known copy number (x-axis) and the corresponding Cq value (y-axis).•The curve allows for linear regression analysis, which is then used to calculate the unknown RNA concentration in test samples based on their Cq values.

steps.title: Collect and store wastewater sample
steps.instruction: Collect 5 mL aliquots of raw wastewater (24‑h composite) in sterile tubes, keep on ice/4 °C and process within 48 h.

steps.title: Prepare lysate (NS1/NS2)
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL NucliSENS® lysis buffer to the 5 mL wastewater aliquot, vortex at high speed (settings 7–8) for 1 min, then incubate at room temperature for 10 min. The resulting mixture is the lysate.

steps.title: Neutral phenol‑chloroform extraction (NS2 only)
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL conical tube place a separation tube containing 4 g of high‑vacuum silicon grease + silicon dioxide (90:10 w/w). Transfer 15 mL lysate into the separation tube, add 15 mL phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1, pH 7.8–8.2, Sigma‑Aldrich Ref 77617), shake vigorously by hand for 1 min, centrifuge 3500 × g for 5 min, and transfer the upper aqueous phase (≈15 mL) to a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Centrifugation step (NS1 only)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 2500 × g for 5 min, transfer the supernatant (≈14.5 mL) to a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Bind RNA to magnetic silica beads
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL magnetic silica beads (from the NucliSENS® kit) to the aqueous phase (or supernatant), vortex at high speed (7–8) for 1 min, incubate at room temperature for 10 min, place the tube on a magnetic rack and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Wash and elute beads (miniMAG option)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the beads in 400 µL Wash Buffer 1 (WB1) and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube placed in the NucliSENS® miniMAG™. Perform two washes with WB1 (30 s contact each, aspirate after each), then two washes with 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 (WB2) (30 s contact each), then a final wash with 500 µL Wash Buffer 3 (WB3) for 15 s. Remove the tube, resuspend beads in 50 µL WB3, elute at 60 °C for 5 min while shaking at 1400 rpm in a Thermomixer Comfort, place on magnetic rack and collect the 50 µL eluate.

steps.title: Wash and elute beads (easyMAG option)
steps.instruction: Load the bead suspension onto the NucliSENS® easyMAG® system; the instrument automatically performs the same WB1, WB2, WB3 washes and elutes RNA in 50 µL WB3.

steps.title: Wash and elute beads (manual option)
steps.instruction: Using a magnetic rack, manually repeat the WB1, WB2, and WB3 washing steps described for the miniMAG, then elute in 50 µL WB3 as above.

steps.title: Optional column purification (NS protocols)
steps.instruction: Place a Zymo‑Spin™ III‑HRC column into a collection tube, add 600 µL Prep‑solution, centrifuge 8000 × g for 3 min, transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL tube, load the 50 µL eluate, centrifuge 16000 × g for 3 min, and collect the flow‑through RNA for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Sample preparation for Z protocol
steps.instruction: Mix 350 µL Water Concentrating Buffer™ with 5 mL wastewater, vortex 1 min, incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect pellet (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 3000 × g for 15 min, carefully remove the supernatant leaving ≈250 µL of pellet.

steps.title: Lysis and bead beating (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Add 750 µL DNA/RNA Shield™ to the pellet, vortex 1 min, transfer the 1 mL suspension to a ZR BashingBead™ Lysis Tube, bead‑beat in a Vortex‑Genie 2 for 1 min at high speed (7–8), then centrifuge 12000 × g for 2 min.

steps.title: RNA binding to column (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Collect 400 µL supernatant, mix with an equal volume of RNA Binding Buffer, vortex 30 s, transfer to a Zymo‑Spin™ IIICG column, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of absolute ethanol to the flow‑through, vortex 30 s, transfer to a new Zymo‑Spin™ IIICG column, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s.

steps.title: Wash and elution preparation (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer to the column, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s, move the column to a new RNase‑free tube, add 100 µL DNase/RNase‑Free Water, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s.

steps.title: Final purification with III‑HRC filter (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Place a Zymo‑Spin™ III‑HRC filter into a fresh collection tube, add 600 µL Prep Solution, centrifuge 8000 × g for 3 min, discard flow‑through, transfer the eluate from the previous step onto the filter, centrifuge 16000 × g for 3 min.

steps.title: Second binding and column purification (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Mix the filtrate with 200 µL RNA Binding Buffer and 300 µL absolute ethanol, load onto a Zymo‑Spin™ IC column in a collection tube, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash RNA column (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s; wash with 700 µL RNA Wash Buffer, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s, discard; wash again with 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer, centrifuge 16000 × g for 2 min.

steps.title: Final elution (Z protocol)
steps.instruction: Transfer the column into a RNase‑free tube, add 50 µL DNase/RNase‑Free Water, centrifuge 16000 × g for 30 s. The eluate contains purified RNA.

steps.title: Store extracted RNA
steps.instruction: Aliquot the RNA and store at –80 °C until RT‑qPCR analysis.

steps.title: Prepare RT‑qPCR reaction
steps.instruction: In a 20 µL reaction using the RNA UltraSens™ One‑Step kit, combine 2 µL extracted RNA, primers (1 µM targeting the SARS‑CoV‑2 E gene), probe (0.3 µM), and the kit’s master mix as instructed.

steps.title: Run RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Program a Bio‑Rad CFX96™ cycler: 50 °C 30 min (RT), 95 °C 5 min (initial denaturation), then 45 cycles of 95 °C 15 s and 58 °C 40 s. Acquire Cq values.

steps.title: Generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10‑fold serial dilution series of the SARS‑CoV‑2 E‑gene plasmid (pCR2.1, Invitrogen), run each dilution in the RT‑qPCR assay, plot log(copy number) vs Cq, and use the linear regression for quantifying unknown samples.

steps.title: Determine LOD and LOQ
steps.instruction: Using Twist Bioscience Synthetic SARS‑CoV‑2 RNA Control 2, define the limit of detection as 10 genome copies (GC) per reaction (≥95 % detection in 6 replicates) and the limit of quantification as 10 GC per reaction with a coefficient of variation ≤25 %.

steps.title: Assess RT‑qPCR inhibition
steps.instruction: Run each RNA extract undiluted and at 1:10 dilution, compare Cq values; calculate ΔCq. If ΔCq ≥ 2.3, inhibition ≈ 50 %; if ΔCq ≥ 1.3, inhibition ≈ 75 %. Inhibition up to 75 % is acceptable per ISO 15216‑1.

description: The comparison was performed in parallel in three laboratories; each laboratory compared protocol Z designed for environmental samples to one of the three others (SB, NS1 or NS2) (Fig. 1). Three comparative sets were prepared: Z versus NS1 (Laboratory 1), Z versus NS2 (Laboratory 2), and Z versus SB (Laboratory 3). Each laboratory used raw WW samples collected in three WWTPs with three distinct samples per WWTP (n = 9 per laboratory) (Table 1). As each sample underwent five technical replicates, the comparative set of each lab contained a total of 45 data and the global dataset contained 135 data. The comparison of the RNA extraction protocols was based on two key factors: the quantification of the SARS-CoV-2 RNA and the removal of RT-qPCR inhibitors by targeting FRNAPH belonging to genogroup II (FRNAPH GGII). The molecular biology analyses were performed as previously described in the original research article [1]. RT-qPCR inhibition was estimated for each sample of extracted RNA by comparing the quantification cycle (Cq) values obtained for the undiluted extract with those of the 1/10 diluted extract. If the difference between the two Cq values (ΔCq) reached 2.3, then the inhibition was 50 %. If this difference reached 1.3, then the inhibition was 75 %. According to ISO 152616-1 (2017) on the genome quantification of noroviruses and hepatitis A virus in food and bottled water matrices, up to 75 % inhibition is acceptable. Statistical analyses were performed using GraphPad - Prism software (version 9.5.0). Each laboratory compared two extraction protocols on paired samples. The Wilcoxon test (n = 2 series) was employed to compare viral RNA genome copies and RT-qPCR inhibitor removal for the dataset of each lab. Negative samples were included in the statistical comparison, and the Logrank test for paired samples (n = 2 series) was applied in this case.
